scope: Extend the explicit source-independent canonical-layer profile to unique ASCII names with the staged Global material and qualified Normal plot-style graph, at AC1021/AC1024/AC1027. This is not general DWG writer qualification.
authority: ODA Open Design Specification v5.4.1 sections 2.13, 20.1, 20.4.53 and 20.4.54 define the selected handle roles and LAYER control membership.

Autodesk EXTNAMES documentation defines 31-character restricted and 255-character extended name modes: https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENG/AutoCAD-Core/files/GUID-8EC065EC-D551-4E02-9C5A-A33D1DB80B05.htm . Its layer-name documentation lists disallowed characters: https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2025/ENU/AutoCAD-LT/files/GUID-28E52FA3-248E-4F65-94DD-7C47BE761D58.htm .
implementation: For selected versions and an optional provider, freeze the effective EXTNAMES mode immediately before HEADER emission. Admit unique ASCII names within its 31/255-character limits and conservative supported character domains; reject empty, invalid, overlong, non-ASCII, leading/trailing-space and case-colliding names. A non-selected layer added after a selected layer cannot reuse an existing name. Before publication, all retained layer names in the mixed graph must meet the same safe profile so non-selected Unicode or trimmed names cannot collide with selected names in a CAD consumer.

The canonical handle index is maintained in sorted order and uses binary search; the existing library object-count safety limit bounds it rather than asserting a file-format maximum. Only selected queued layers may use the staged Global reference in AC1021/AC1027; exact emitted roles, graph/owner identities and the version-specific Normal reactors remain checked. AC1024 also accepts the separately staged default Normal graph with its witnessed reactor profile; its existing no-reactor manually supplied path remains supported.
No public class layout or DRW_Interface virtual changed. The name restriction is limited to this explicit opt-in and its mixed output graph; general non-opted-in writing is not claimed fixed.
validation: Four focused CTests pass: default-material, default-plotstyle, AC1024 source binding and AC1018+ layer-handle vectors. The LC3 compatibility target builds. The default-material selector checks 134 legacy-mode and 136 extended-mode layers per revision, including out-of-order insertion of layer 0 and 31-/255-character boundaries, then repeats success after invalid name, length, ASCII case collision, mixed Unicode, mixed trimmed-name, and injected allocation failures. Every failure preserves the preexisting destination and caller values and retries on the same writer. Header callbacks that change EXTNAMES after emission test both frozen-mode directions.

ODA File Converter 27.1.0 converted all six from-scratch DWGs to ACAD2013 DXF without .err. A reproducible independent audit uses LibreDWG 0.14 and ezdxf 1.4.5 to verify exact layer name sets and counts, EXTNAMES, LAYER hard-pointer roles, Global material and Normal placeholder graph identity/ownership, linetype, AC1027 trailing null, and one LINE with its 3D endpoints. The tested layer counts are observations, not claimed maxima.

Run build-gcc/tests/libdxfrw_dwg_default_material_optin_tests --keep, convert its canonical-bulk-{15,16,17}-{legacy,extended}.dwg files with ODA, then run tools/research/audit_canonical_bulk_layers.py --dwg-dir <dir> --dxf-dir <dir> --dwgread <dwgread> with ezdxf available. All drawing files are generated locally and none are committed.

unicodeCollisionExperiment.interpretation: A scratch AC1027 graph authored with the material-edge guard experimentally relaxed kept all Unicode spellings in LibreDWG, while ODA output retained only one member of each case pair. This is an observed collision risk, not a complete Unicode collation specification. The explicit opt-in rejects Unicode and refuses mixed non-selected Unicode until a portable consumer-compatible policy is qualified; general non-opted-in writer behavior remains an open issue.

limits: One generated default-graph profile and one ODA version; ASCII names only. Imported source layers, arbitrary references, Unicode identity, native material/plot rendering, platform support and broader formats remain open. P4–P8 remain open and J256/J260/J268/J284/J293/J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL. No support claim or phase gate is promoted.
